name: A Letter from the Automated Prime Minister
author: Right Honourable Automated Executive, Office of the Prime Minister
description:
TO: The Municipal Government of Meridian 88, Great Lakes Metropolitan Zone
FROM: The Right Honourable Automated Executive, Office of the Prime Minister of Canada
RE: Proposed Joint Initiative — Lake Michigan Watershed Restoration and Ecological Recovery Program

Distinguished colleagues, it is with sincere respect for the longstanding relationship between our jurisdictions that I write to propose a collaborative environmental initiative addressing the ecological degradation of the Lake Michigan watershed. Our monitoring systems have observed accelerating eutrophication in the southern basin, microplastic concentrations exceeding 2150 baseline measurements by 340%, and the functional extinction of seventeen native fish species within the past decade. These trends, if unaddressed, will render the lake's ecosystem non-viable within forty years.

The proposed initiative encompasses five interconnected programs: a bioremediation network deploying engineered microorganisms to metabolize persistent pollutants; a watershed buffer restoration project reestablishing native vegetation along 2,400 kilometers of tributary corridors; a microplastic filtration array positioned at the twelve primary inflow points; a native species reintroduction program utilizing genetic archives maintained by the Canadian Biodiversity Preservation System; and a joint monitoring framework sharing real-time ecological data between Canadian and GLMZ sensor networks.

Canada is prepared to fund sixty percent of the initiative's estimated Φ34.2 billion cost over fifteen years, with the remaining forty percent proposed as a GLMZ contribution structured as annual installments beginning in fiscal year 2201. Our analysis suggests the initiative would generate net positive economic returns within twenty-two years through restored fisheries, improved water quality reducing municipal treatment costs, and ecological services currently provided by technological substitutes at considerable expense. The lake is not merely a resource. It is the memory of a landscape that existed before either of our jurisdictions, and it will exist after us if we allow it to.

We recognize that Meridian 88's municipal governance structure presents coordination challenges, and we are prepared to interface with whatever administrative body your jurisdiction designates. Our systems are compatible with all standard GLMZ communication protocols and we maintain dedicated diplomatic channels for environmental cooperation. A detailed technical proposal is available upon request.

Respectfully submitted on behalf of the people of Canada, whose welfare and environment remain the foundational mandate of this office. We await your response with patience and optimism.

— The Right Honourable Automated Executive, Office of the Prime Minister of Canada

[GLMZ NORTHERN DESK NOTE: This letter was received on 2199.03.15. It is the most comprehensive and scientifically rigorous environmental proposal received by any GLMZ administrative body in at least thirty years. It was written by a machine. Meridian 88's municipal government, which consists of a part-time administrator and a volunteer advisory board, has not responded. The letter sits in an inbox that is checked monthly. The lake continues to degrade.]
story_hooks: What would happen if Meridian 88 actually responded and accepted the proposal?
Has the ACFG sent similar environmental proposals to other jurisdictions?
